notes: Thresholds for every dashboard metric. Bands are data: lo/hi (null = unbounded) with explicit inclusive flags. Read by metric_guide.py (this dashboard and synkhos/factory#172). Edit here, no code change needed.

cache_hit_rate.label: Cache hit rate
cache_hit_rate.note: a floor, not a target — 100% is not a goal (every turn adds new context)
cache_hit_rate.meaning: Share of input tokens served from the prompt cache; high means contexts are being reused instead of rebuilt.
cache_hit_rate.action: Contexts are being rebuilt — idle gaps past the 5-min cache TTL, changing early prompt content, or many tiny sessions.

context_per_call.label: Context per call
context_per_call.note: tokens read per model call: (input + cache write + cache read) / calls
context_per_call.meaning: How much context each call re-reads; high means long sessions are dragging a big history through every turn.
context_per_call.action: Each call re-reads a large context — 71% of spend was cache reads in late Sept. Start fresh sessions per task, compact earlier, push exploration into sub-agents.

context_growth.label: Context growth
context_growth.note: ratio of mean context on late calls (21+) to early calls (1-5) within a session
context_growth.meaning: How much bigger the context is late in a session than early; a high ratio means sessions run long past the point of useful history.
context_growth.action: Sessions are growing well past their early size — end sessions at natural task boundaries, /compact sooner, or restart with a short summary.

output_share.label: Output share
output_share.note: agentic work is naturally low; shown for context
output_share.meaning: Share of all tokens that the model wrote; agentic work is naturally low because most tokens are re-read context.

durable_merge_rate.label: Durable-merge rate
durable_merge_rate.note: merged PRs with no revert or reopen within 14 days
durable_merge_rate.meaning: Share of merged PRs that stuck; low means work is being reverted or reopened.
durable_merge_rate.action: Merged work is being reverted or reopened — tighten review and tests before merging, and look at which PRs bounced back.

rework_share.label: Rework share
rework_share.note: ci-fix and conflict $ over implementation $ (no data until synkhos/factory#109)
rework_share.meaning: How much spend goes into fixing CI and conflicts instead of building; high means the first attempt keeps failing.
rework_share.action: Too much spend goes to fixing what was just built — sharpen specs and acceptance checks so the first pass lands.

dead_end_share.label: Dead-end share
dead_end_share.note: dead-end $ over total spend in the same (Me) scope
dead_end_share.meaning: Share of spend that went into work later closed not-planned or abandoned on a stale branch.
dead_end_share.action: Spend is going to work that never ships — kill doomed issues earlier and check scope before starting long sessions.

validity_rho.label: Points validity (rho)
validity_rho.note: Spearman rho between complexity points and attributed $; fewer than 15 rated issues is always low confidence
validity_rho.meaning: Whether bigger-point issues really cost more; high means the point ratings are trustworthy.
validity_rho.action: Point ratings do not track cost — recalibrate the rater before trusting $/pt.

cost_per_point.label: $ per point
cost_per_point.note: median $/pt in the latest ISO week with shipped rated issues vs the median of the 4 weeks before it
cost_per_point.meaning: What a complexity point costs now compared with the recent past; lower is better.
cost_per_point.action: $/pt is rising versus the last 4 weeks — check for dead ends, oversized sessions or model choice.

throughput.label: Throughput
throughput.note: points shipped in the latest ISO week with shipped rated issues vs the mean of the 4 weeks before it
throughput.meaning: Points shipped compared with the recent weekly average; higher is better.
throughput.action: Shipping has slowed versus the last 4 weeks — look for blocked issues or time lost to rework.
